title: autopilot step 1 of the ledger removal: branch updates use GitHub's compare-and-swap and then fast-forward the local task ref, with no once() ledger entry
acceptance: State defaults. The defaults list at bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:60-62 gains `poll_seq=0`, `retries={}`, `holds={}` and `updates={}`, so an existing state.json gets them on first load. `poll()` (fm_autopilot.py:385) increments `data['poll_seq']` as its very first statement, before the `policy_error` early return at :386-388 and before any read. So a poll that returns early on a policy error, or is later cut short by `network_failure` (:231-238; the catch in `poll()` is at :433-434), still advances it. Every delay below counts in `poll_seq` steps.

Update-branch by predicate and CAS. The trigger is an open PR observed with `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: behind`, and not a draft. `mergeable: null` means unknown, never behind. Today's check is fm_autopilot.py:374-382.
The update is not attempted while a worker or reviewer round for the task is live (`fm_concurrent.live_rounds`, bin/lib/fm_concurrent.py:63-91), or while an autopilot job for the task is busy (`busy()`, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:102-104). It is re-decided on a later poll, with no wake. Otherwise, on that trigger the autopilot calls `gh api -X PUT repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}/update-branch -f expected_head_sha=<observed head> --include` through a new method `Pilot.probe(argv) -> (rc, stdout, stderr)`. Unlike `command()` (:114-122), `probe` never raises on a non-zero exit, so the status line, body and exit code can be read. The local-ref sync's git calls below go through the same `probe`. `fm_binding.fetch_ref(runner=…)` expects a runner that returns stdout and raises on failure (bin/lib/fm_binding.py:23-33), so the sync passes `runner=self.checked`. `Pilot.checked(argv)` is a thin adapter: it calls `probe` and raises ValueError carrying the argv and the last non-empty stderr line on a non-zero exit, and otherwise returns stdout. `fetch_ref`'s own `finally: update-ref -d <private ref>` still runs through that runner. The existing `fetch_ref` callers keep their contract unchanged: fm_autopilot.py:291, fm_autopilot_loop.py:75, fm_stack.py:89 and fm_binding.py:119. The cleanup and error regressions at tests/private-fetch.test.sh:86 and :103 still pass.
Reading the answer. `probe` returns `gh api --include` output: an HTTP status line, header lines, a blank line, then the JSON body. The status is read from the status line, never from the exit code: `gh api` exits 1 on any status of 400 or more, and still prints the headers and body.
- 202: store `data['updates'][n] = {head, seq}`. While the observed head is unchanged and fewer than 20 polls have passed, no further PUT is made.
- 422 whose body contains 'expected head sha' (case-insensitive): someone else moved the head. No wake, no retry, re-decide next poll.
- Any other answer (another 422, 403, 5xx, no status line, a transport error): do the PR re-read below, then decide.
The PR re-read is defined as the same call today's update uses before writing: `gh pr view <n> --repo <repo> --json headRefOid,mergeable,mergeStateStatus` (fm_autopilot.py:377-378). It goes through `self.command` (raising), not `self.api`, so no ETag cache can hand back a stale head. It runs only after a non-202 answer that is not the 'expected head sha' 422. It reads `headRefOid` only:
- different from `expected_head_sha`: 'moved', with no wake, no retry, and a re-decision next poll;
- equal: the failure was not a move, so it is a retry as below;
- the re-read itself fails (it raises): retry as below.
No `once(['update', …])` entry is written. Update errors are caught per PR inside `pull()` and never reach `poll()`'s `network_failure`.

Local ref sync, before advance. In `pull()`, before `self.advance(...)` (fm_autopilot.py:342), the autopilot reads the local task ref `refs/heads/<pr.head.ref>` and compares it with the observed PR head.
- Equal: advance as today, with no fetch.
- Missing: create it at the PR head after a private fetch whose sha equals the observed head (`update-ref refs/heads/<branch> <head> ""`, which only creates). If the fetched sha differs from the observed head, the moved-during-fetch rule below applies. There is no unpublished work to protect.
- Different: fetch the PR head with `fm_binding.fetch_ref` (as `prepare_head` does, fm_autopilot_loop.py:70-78), then compare the fetched sha with the observed PR head, the way `prepare_head` does (fm_autopilot_loop.py:75-78). If they differ, the PR moved during the fetch (a force-push): that PR's advance is skipped for this poll, nothing is created or moved, and it is neither a retry nor a wake. It is re-decided next poll from the new observation. Only when they are equal, run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <local> <head>`. Exit 0 means ancestor, exit 1 means not an ancestor, anything else is an error. On an ancestor, fast-forward only when all three hold:
  - no worker or reviewer round for the task is live (`fm_concurrent.live_rounds`, bin/lib/fm_concurrent.py:63-91);
  - no autopilot job for the task is busy (`busy()`, fm_autopilot_loop.py:102-104);
  - the task worktree on that branch, if any, is clean (`status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` is empty). The worktree is found by `git worktree list --porcelain`, as bin/lib/fm_stack.py:57,106-113 does.
  The fast-forward is `git -C <worktree> merge --ff-only <head>` when there is a worktree, else `git update-ref refs/heads/<branch> <head> <old>`. After a successful fast-forward, advance proceeds in the same poll.
- Not an ancestor (unpublished work): unchanged. Advance runs, and its stale-ref refusal (fm_binding.py:121) parks and wakes, because that needs judgment.
- Hold: an ancestor with a failed condition. `advance` is skipped for that PR on that poll, and nothing parks.
  - When the only failing condition is a busy autopilot job, the hold is silent and does not count. That job is the autopilot's own: a gate job, which can still run on the old head after a 202, because `advance` (:342) runs before the update block (:374-382) in the same `pull()`. It ends on its own, and today `advance` already returns quietly while busy (fm_autopilot_loop.py:148).
  - When a worker or reviewer round for the task is live, the hold is also silent and does not count, matching today's silent wait in `advance` (fm_autopilot_loop.py:150-152); firstmate's own manual update during a review round (skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:305) therefore raises no wake.
  - Only a dirty task worktree counts: `data['holds'][n] = {head, count}` increments on each such poll, and when count reaches 3, one wake `ffhold-<n>-<head>` names the dirty worktree.
- Sync errors: any fetch, rev-parse, merge-base, worktree or fast-forward command error, including merge-base exits other than 0 and 1. That PR's advance is skipped for the poll, and the error goes into the retry record `sync:<n>:<head>` below. It never reaches `advance-error` (:343-345) or `network_failure`.
- Every poll starts with step 1, the equal-ref check, whatever retry record exists. If the local ref now equals the PR head (for example firstmate repaired it by hand), any `sync:<n>:<head>` record and any hold for that PR are cleared and advance runs in that same poll. Otherwise: a sync record whose 3 attempts are spent skips advance silently (its one wake was already queued); a record whose `due_seq` is still ahead skips advance silently for that poll; a due record makes the next attempt.

The test sets the dict to the PR head before each pull, at about 96, 100, 105, 108 and 112 (heads 'a' then 'b'), the same way `autopilot_cases.py` does with `pull_at`. In autopilot_loop.py, only the `c…` pull at about 340 uses `pull_at`; the `advance(PR)` at about 338 is unchanged.
